name: Hammer union
function: The three-piece quick connection on flow iron: a male sub, a female sub with a seal ring, and a threaded wing nut that is tightened with a hammer.

tabs.overview: The wing nut has three lugs that are struck with a sledge to make up and break out. Pressure classes are identified by figure numbers that are vendor nomenclature; halves of different figure numbers can thread together in some sizes and will fail under pressure. Color coding and thread checks are used to prevent mismatches.
tabs.engineering: Rated by figure number to the pressure class of the line; seal rings are elastomer with a metal backup on high-pressure unions.
tabs.safety: Never mix union halves across pressure classes even if they thread together. Never strike a union under pressure. Hands clear of the lugs when hammering.
tabs.evidence: API 6A (S1) for pressure-containing parts and connections; public OEM pages (S2, S3, S5, S11, S12) for configurations; field and manufacturing practice (S9).

hazards.control: Pressure test before pumping; bleed down and verify zero before breaking any connection.
Restraints and whip checks on iron; exclusion zone around pressurized lines.
Hands clear of wing nuts, handwheels, and actuator linkages during operation.
